paragraphs: Rabbi Ila said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Zevachim 8b; Challon 81b: Rabbi Ila in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. But Maharshal reads in Rabbi Yehudah’s name in Rav’s name, Nedarim 7b; Arakhin 7a; beginning of Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah. Rabbi Ila said, “A person is known by three things: his purse,” etc., Haddar. Our reading, however, has Rav Chama saying it. Know that the Jerusalem Talmud calls him Hila, Hilai, or Rabbi La. He died in the first Adar, Jerusalem Talmud, Ha'omer, halakhah 2. Gefer is a well between Ein Zeitim and Safed; near the olives is a mound where Rabbi Ila is buried (Gelilot Eretz Yisrael [גא״י; expansion provisional]). Rabbi Ivo bar Naggara before him. Rabbi Avin asked before him and spoke in his name. Rabbi Avin bar Kahana asked him. Rabbi Avun bar Chiyya asked, Demai, chapter 1, halakhah 2. In Rabbi Avina’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Yevamot, chapter 3; Rabbi Le'azar’s name, Ma'aserot, chapter 3; Rabbi Lazar’s name, and in his name, Terumot, chapter 2. Rabbi Bisna in his name. In Rabbi Hoshaya’s name, Yevamot, chapter 13. Rabbi Ze'ira, in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name. Ze'ira praised him and called him “builder of the Torah,” Jerusalem Talmud, Hamemuneh, halakhah 5; Rabbi Chaggai, Ha'omer, halakhah 2. Rabbi Chizkiyah in his name. In Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa’s name, Chagigah 21b; Chalfai’s name, Ma'aserot, chapter 3. Rabbi Chanina, Rabbi Ammi, and Rabbi Assi when Rav Huna’s coffin came. In Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Mi Shehayah Tamei and beginning of Chomer Bakkodesh. Rabbi Yonah in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, chapter 1. Rabbi Yonatan ben Hila; Rabbi Yose in his name, Kilayim, chapter 1, halakhah 7; Shekalim, chapter 4. In Rabbi Yannai’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Hamafkid and Ketubbot, chapter 1; Rabbi Yosa’s name, Gittin, chapter 1. Rabbi Nachum, his brother. Rabbi Simon bar Zavda before him. Rabbi Pinchas in his name. He was ascending Rabbah bar Shila’s stairs, Chagigah 5b. Rabbi Redifa in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, chapter 1. In Shmuel’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Mi Shehayah Tamei; Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, Shekalim, chapter 7. Rabbi Shimon bar Yisina in his name; in Rabbi Shimon bar Yosina’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, chapter 13; Resh Lakish’s name. He delivered a discourse over Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid when he died.
